# Single cell protein (SCP)

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Single cell protein (SCP)** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Single cell protein (SCP)

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

**Single cell protein** is edible protein from microbes — bacteria, yeast, fungi, algae — grown on cheap substrates (whey, molasses, straw, even petroleum wastes). The name is a marketing choice: 'microbial protein' sounded unappetising. SCP can supply protein without farmland: a 250-kg cow gains ~200 g of protein per day; the same mass of microbes can produce tonnes of protein in hours.

**Concept flow — why microbes as food (study in this order)**

| Step | Concept | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The protein gap | Growing population vs limited cropland and pasture |
| 2 | Microbes' speed | Doubling in minutes-hours vs months for animals; huge biomass fast |
| 3 | Cheap substrates | Whey, molasses, waste starch, methanol — value added to waste |
| 4 | Product | Protein-rich biomass (60–80% protein dry weight) with vitamins and minerals |
| 5 | Uses | Human food supplements, animal feed (e.g. Spirulina, Quorn mycoprotein) |
| 6 | Limitations | Consumer acceptance, nucleic-acid content, quality control |

**SCP sources — microbe, substrate and product**

| Microbe | Type | Substrate | Product / use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spirulina | Cyanobacterium (blue-green alga) | Open ponds, alkaline water | Health-food supplement; traditional food (Chad dihe) |
| Chlorella | Green alga | Sunlight + CO2 in ponds | Protein and vitamin supplement |
| Saccharomyces / Candida | Yeasts | Molasses, whey, petroleum fractions | Animal feed, baker's/brewer's yeast biomass |
| Fusarium venenatum | Filamentous fungus | Glucose syrup | Quorn mycoprotein — the commercial SCP success |
| Methylophilus | Methylotrophic bacterium | Methanol | High-protein feed; ~25 g protein per 100 g growth in hours |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — the speed comparison.** A 250-kg cow adds about 200 g of protein per day. Microbial biomass doubling in ~2 hours means the same 250 kg of microbes, growing exponentially, can produce roughly 25 tonnes of protein in a single day (given substrate and oxygen). That 100,000× speed advantage is the entire argument for SCP — and why it matters most where land, not money, is the constraint.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Definition: protein from MICROBIAL biomass (Spirulina, Methylophilus methylotrophus, yeast, Chlorella) grown on waste — the microbe names are the marks.
Trick 2: Merits: high protein (Spirulina >50%), fast growth (microbes double in hours), uses waste substrate, little land/water — four merits.
Trick 3: 250 kg cow vs 250 g microbe comparison: microbe produces ~25 tonnes protein/day vs cow 200 g — the classic numerical contrast.
Trick 4: Limitation: public acceptance, texture/taste, contamination control — one line for the balanced answer.
